findings.current: I could see Jongni Chu’s eyes widened in astonishment.
findings.defect: The verb form is ungrammatical after “could see.”
findings.rationale: The bare infinitive “widen” is required in this construction and preserves the action and viewpoint.
findings.replacement: I could see Jongni Chu’s eyes widen in astonishment.

findings.current: Even with my seventh-tier grades, I knew the law of universal gravitation.
findings.defect: “Seventh-tier grades” is an unnatural and unclear English collocation.
findings.rationale: The replacement clarifies that Taekyung means his academic performance while preserving the specified tier and the self-deprecating joke.
findings.replacement: Even though my school grades were in the seventh tier, I knew the law of universal gravitation.

findings.current: The Sect Leaders of the Beggars’ Sect and Kunlun Sect—two sects renowned for their movement techniques—disappeared with their disciples in tow.
findings.defect: The appositive is grammatically attached to the Sect Leaders but describes the sects, producing a momentary category mismatch.
findings.rationale: This makes the appositive’s referent explicit without changing who departs or why those groups lead the pursuit.
findings.replacement: The leaders of the Beggars’ Sect and Kunlun Sect—both sects renowned for their movement techniques—disappeared with their disciples in tow.
